paragraphs: Masked diffusion models generate sequences by filling in missing tokens. A single model evaluation can contain useful information about several missing positions, yet standard sampling procedures may leave some of that information unused. This paper observes that a partially completed sequence often already determines multiple remaining tokens, creating an opportunity to fill them together.

The proposed EB-Sampler decides dynamically how many tokens to reveal in one evaluation. Its entropy-bounded rule uses a predefined approximate error tolerance to control this decision. The idea is to exploit predictions that carry little uncertainty while accounting for the error introduced by accelerated unmasking. The authors also place the method within a broader family of adaptive samplers and provide an error analysis that motivates its design.

On the reported coding and mathematical reasoning benchmarks, EB-Sampler speeds up sampling from leading masked diffusion models by roughly two to three times without reducing performance. Tests on maze navigation and sudoku also support the procedure. The contribution is a replacement sampler that extracts more useful work from each model evaluation.
neurips-2025-accelerated-sampling-from-m.tldr: EB-Sampler adaptively reveals multiple tokens per model evaluation, achieving roughly two to three times faster sampling on reported benchmarks without performance loss.

paragraphs: Gradient-based explanations use a model's sensitivity to its input to help show which parts influence its output. These explanations can be noisy and difficult to interpret. SmoothGrad addresses this by adding Gaussian noise during gradient smoothing, but the amount of noise is commonly chosen manually or through a heuristic.

This paper examines how smoothing can itself introduce unwanted noise. It connects that problem to out-of-range samples generated during the smoothing process. AdaptGrad uses this connection to adapt the sampling procedure, controlling out-of-range sampling with the aim of reducing the extra noise. Its central contribution is therefore a way to make the smoothing process more responsive to the source of the artifacts it can produce.

The authors report qualitative and quantitative experiments in which AdaptGrad could remove almost all noise from the original gradients compared with baseline methods. These findings support its use for clearer gradient visualizations. The abstract presents the method as simple and broadly applicable to gradient-based interpretation, with the reported benefit centered on reducing noise in the resulting explanations.
neurips-2025-adaptgrad-adaptive-sampling.tldr: AdaptGrad adapts gradient smoothing to control out-of-range sampling and reduce noise in model explanation visualizations.

paragraphs: Autonomous driving systems need testing on dangerous traffic situations, but real-world datasets contain relatively few of these rare events. Adv-BMT addresses this shortage by augmenting recorded scenarios with realistic, varied adversarial interactions. The goal is to supply challenging situations that can help evaluate and train driving systems.

The framework constructs scenarios in two stages. It first creates adversarial initializations, then uses a bidirectional motion transformer to predict traffic motion backward. Starting from the scenario's final frame, the model reconstructs earlier frames until it reaches the beginning. This reverses the usual chronological prediction direction and provides a way to generate the traffic interactions leading into a challenging final situation.

The authors report that realistic and diverse collision interactions can be generated without collision data for pretraining. In their experiments, training with the augmented dataset reduces episode collision rates by 20% compared with previous work. This result connects scenario generation to a downstream training benefit, suggesting that the generated interactions provide useful experience with situations that ordinary driving datasets rarely capture.
neurips-2025-adv-bmt-bidirectional-motio.tldr: Adv-BMT generates challenging traffic scenarios backward from final frames, with augmented training reducing episode collision rates by 20% in the reported comparison.

paragraphs: Language models can depend on misleading associations and produce hallucinated content. This paper proposes Causality-driven Robust Optimization, or CdRO, to address these problems through selective parameter updates. Its aim is to strengthen components associated with causal reasoning while preserving useful pretrained knowledge and reducing overfitting.

CdRO compares how parameter matrices behave during training on original examples, counterfactual variants, and paraphrases. These comparisons feed a lightweight logistic regression model that is updated in real time to identify relevant components dynamically. The selected parameters are then trained with an enhanced policy optimization algorithm whose reward encourages both generalization and robustness. This makes the choice of what to update part of the optimization process itself.

Experiments across multiple tasks and twelve language models report superior performance, reduced reliance on spurious associations, and fewer hallucinations. The findings support the authors' approach of directing training toward components identified through these data comparisons. The stated outcome is improved resilience and mitigation of hallucinations, rather than their complete elimination.
neurips-2025-boosting-resilience-of-larg.tldr: CdRO dynamically selects and trains language-model components associated with causal reasoning to reduce spurious associations and hallucinations.

paragraphs: Camouflaged objects blend into their surroundings, making it difficult to identify their boundaries across video frames. Although SAM2 has advanced video segmentation, its performance on camouflage remains weaker, especially with simple point or box prompts. CamSAM2 adds components that help handle these scenes while leaving SAM2's existing parameters unchanged.

A dedicated decamouflaged token allows features to be adjusted for this task. Two object-aware fusion modules bring together detailed, high-resolution information from the current frame and earlier frames. A further component forms and remembers object prototypes using high-quality features from previous frames. Together, these additions let the system draw on both present visual evidence and stored information about the object.

Across three camouflage segmentation datasets, the authors report substantial improvements while adding very few learnable parameters. With the Hiera-T backbone, gains include 12.2 mDice on MoCA-Mask with a click prompt and 19.6 mDice on SUN-SEG-Hard with a mask prompt. These results show that targeted feature adjustment and temporal information can substantially improve SAM2's performance in the evaluated camouflage settings.
neurips-2025-camsam2-segment-anything-ac.tldr: CamSAM2 adds lightweight feature adjustment and temporal object information to improve camouflage segmentation while keeping SAM2's original parameters fixed.

paragraphs: Chemistry draws on many forms of knowledge, from molecular notation and diagrams to textbooks, research articles, and executable code. ChemPile is a 250 GB dataset designed to bring these materials together for general-purpose chemical foundation models. It contains more than 75 billion tokens of curated chemical data for training and evaluation.

The collection follows a progression from introductory learning to specialized expertise. It includes educational material, scientific text, problem-solving traces, code, chemical images, and structured representations such as SMILES, SELFIES, IUPAC names, and InChI. This breadth matters because the resource represents chemistry through multiple content types rather than concentrating all training material in one form. Hundreds of hours of expert curation went into its construction.

The authors provide standardized training, validation, and test splits to support comparable evaluation. They also release the dataset through HuggingFace with a consistent API, documentation, and a permissive license. The paper's contribution is this shared data resource and its organization; enabling stronger chemical foundation models is the intended future benefit.
neurips-2025-chempile-a-250-gb-diverse-a.tldr: ChemPile provides over 75 billion tokens of curated, multimodal chemistry data with standardized splits for training and evaluating foundation models.

paragraphs: Continual test-time adaptation updates a model as it encounters unfamiliar data distributions during use. Retaining previous knowledge can prevent forgetting, but historical knowledge can also interfere when the current domain is very different. The paper proposes KFF to manage this tension while learning from a changing stream of test data.

KFF stores class-aware domain knowledge in a paired prompt pool. Its knowledge fission module separates new domain knowledge adaptively, aiming to reduce harmful influence from distinct older domains. This gives the system a way to accommodate differences between domains instead of forcing all incoming information immediately into the same stored representation.

Repeated separation could make the knowledge pool increasingly expensive to maintain. KFF therefore adds a knowledge fusion module that merges newly separated knowledge back into the existing pool. A greedy dynamic merging strategy aims to improve compatibility between old and new knowledge while keeping computation efficient. The contribution is a mechanism for expanding and consolidating domain knowledge, designed to balance adaptation, historical knowledge retention, and storage costs.
neurips-2025-class-aware-domain-knowledg.tldr: KFF separates and merges class-aware domain knowledge to support continual adaptation while limiting harmful historical interference and growing overhead.

paragraphs: Constrained optimization seeks a good solution while respecting requirements on which solutions are allowed. This paper studies that problem through feedback linearization, a technique from nonlinear control. Its main contribution is a rigorous theoretical basis for using this control perspective to develop and analyze optimization methods.

For problems with equality constraints, the authors establish global convergence rates to first-order Karush-Kuhn-Tucker points. These points express first-order conditions involving the objective and its constraints; the stated result concerns reaching such points rather than establishing globally optimal solutions. The analysis also reveals a close relationship between the feedback linearization method and Sequential Quadratic Programming, linking the control formulation to an existing optimization approach.

The authors use that relationship to extend feedback linearization to problems with inequality constraints. They additionally introduce a momentum-accelerated version and prove a convergence guarantee for it. Together, these results show how a control technique can inform a family of constrained optimization algorithms, with theoretical support for their convergence behavior.
neurips-2025-constrained-optimization-fr.tldr: The paper establishes convergence theory for feedback-linearization optimization, connects it to SQP, and develops inequality-constrained and momentum-accelerated extensions.

paragraphs: Coral reef photographs contain information useful for conservation, but interpreting them requires specialist knowledge. CoralVQA turns this challenge into a visual question-answering benchmark, where models answer questions about reef images. Its purpose is to support more accessible interaction with imagery while evaluating understanding of ecological and health-related conditions.

The dataset contains 12,805 real-world images covering 67 coral genera from three oceans, paired with 277,653 questions and answers. A semi-automatic construction pipeline developed with marine biologists combines scalable data production with domain expertise. The emphasis on both specialized annotations and multiple dimensions of questioning addresses requirements that a general image-question dataset may not capture.

The authors evaluate several leading large vision-language models and identify limitations and opportunities for improvement. The resulting contribution is both a specialized evaluation resource and evidence about current model capabilities in this setting. Its conservation relevance lies in supporting the development and assessment of systems that can interpret reef imagery through questions grounded in marine science.
neurips-2025-coralvqa-a-large-scale-visu.tldr: CoralVQA pairs reef images with expert-informed questions and answers to benchmark vision-language understanding for coral monitoring.

paragraphs: Inverse problems recover an unknown signal from measurements that may be noisy or incomplete. Diffusion models can supply prior information about plausible signals, but connecting that prior to the measurements is difficult. Existing approaches described in the paper use heuristic consistency updates or approximate likelihoods, which can produce artifacts and instability in challenging conditions.

C-DPS introduces a stochastic process for the measurements that evolves alongside the diffusion process for the signal. Coupling these two processes allows the authors to derive a closed-form posterior for the preceding signal state, conditioned on the current signal state and the preceding measurement state. Sampling can then proceed recursively using this defined distribution, without the constraint tuning or likelihood approximation targeted by the method.

Across multiple inverse-problem benchmarks, the authors report consistent qualitative and quantitative improvements over existing baselines. The approach matters because it changes how measurement information enters diffusion sampling: the measurements become part of the evolving probabilistic construction. The reported results support this coupling as a way to improve reconstruction.
neurips-2025-coupled-data-and-measuremen.tldr: C-DPS couples signal and measurement diffusion to derive recursive posterior sampling without constraint tuning or likelihood approximation.

paragraphs: An agent following natural-language instructions must connect what a person says to the task it should perform. Flexible wording can create ambiguity across tasks and degrade reinforcement learning performance. DAIL, short for Distributional Aligned Learning, addresses this problem with two components that help distinguish tasks and connect language to behavior.

The first component is a distributional policy. The authors provide theoretical results showing that its value-distribution estimation mechanism improves task differentiability, meaning the ability to distinguish tasks. The second component performs semantic alignment by capturing relationships between trajectories and instructions. Together, these components address both how tasks are represented through their outcomes and how observed behavior corresponds to linguistic descriptions.

Experiments on benchmarks with structured observations and visual observations show better performance than baseline methods. The authors interpret these results as evidence that DAIL effectively resolves instruction ambiguities in the evaluated settings. The contribution is a combined treatment of task distinction and language-behavior correspondence within language-conditioned reinforcement learning, supported by both theoretical analysis and experimental evaluation.
neurips-2025-dail-beyond-task-ambiguity-.tldr: DAIL combines value-distribution estimation and instruction-trajectory alignment to reduce ambiguity in language-conditioned reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: This position paper asks whether foundation models merely make existing scientific work faster or are changing how science is conducted. The authors argue for a transition toward a new scientific paradigm. They organize that argument around the changing role models can play in research, from assisting established workflows to participating in discovery.

Their framework has three stages. Meta-Scientific Integration describes models improving activities within traditional scientific methods. Hybrid Human-AI Co-Creation gives models a collaborative role in defining problems, reasoning, and discovery. Autonomous Scientific Discovery describes models acting as independent agents that generate scientific knowledge with minimal human intervention. The stages distinguish different degrees and forms of participation in the research process.

Using this framework, the paper reviews current applications and emerging capabilities across scientific paradigms, and identifies risks and future directions. Its contribution is an interpretive structure for discussing scientific change. The proposed progression expresses the authors' position on where foundation models are taking science, rather than an experimental demonstration that all three stages have already been achieved.
neurips-2025-foundation-models-for-scien.tldr: This position paper proposes three stages for understanding how foundation models may shift science from assisted workflows toward autonomous discovery.

paragraphs: A drone navigating around moving obstacles must sense and react quickly while operating within limited onboard energy and computation. This paper presents a fully neuromorphic framework for performing navigation and obstacle avoidance using only resources carried by the aircraft. The approach draws inspiration from the efficiency of biological systems.

The framework detects and avoids moving objects without requiring target recognition or trajectory computation. The authors report an overall end-to-end obstacle-avoidance latency of 2.3 milliseconds. This design directly addresses the need for fast responses under the computational constraints of autonomous flight, with the sensing and processing performed onboard rather than depending on external control.

The work also introduces a monocular event-based pose-correction dataset containing more than 50,000 paired and labeled event streams. Validation on an autonomous quadrotor demonstrates reliable navigation and avoidance of diverse obstacles moving at speeds up to 10 meters per second. These results establish a concrete onboard demonstration of the framework, while the dataset provides an additional resource for event-based pose correction.
neurips-2025-fully-autonomous-neuromorph.tldr: A neuromorphic quadrotor system demonstrates fully onboard navigation and moving-obstacle avoidance with 2.3-millisecond overall latency.

paragraphs: Understanding a vision transformer requires explaining both what information it represents and how it processes that information. This paper studies 6,600 features extracted with sparse autoencoders across all layers. The analysis follows the development of representations through the model, providing a systematic view of its internal visual features.

The authors find a progression from simple visual patterns to higher-level semantic content. They also identify specialized feature types associated with curves and spatial positions. To connect these observations to computation, they introduce a residual replacement model that substitutes interpretable features for computations in the residual stream. This produces a simplified circuit intended to remain faithful to the original model while being small enough for human inspection.

The framework therefore links a catalog of internal features to an account of how those features participate in processing. The authors also demonstrate its use in debiasing spurious correlations. That application shows how the interpretation framework can support changes to model behavior, beyond describing what individual features appear to represent.
neurips-2025-interpreting-vision-transfo.tldr: The residual replacement model turns vision-transformer computations into compact, interpretable feature circuits and demonstrates their use in reducing spurious correlations.

paragraphs: Sharpness Aware Minimization, or SAM, trains neural networks by perturbing their parameters before calculating the gradient used for optimization. The aim is to reach regions where the loss changes less sharply with parameter changes. SAM has shown generalization benefits, but obtaining its perturbation requires an additional gradient calculation that doubles computational cost.

Momentum-SAM replaces that gradient-based perturbation direction with the accumulated momentum vector. Inspired by Nesterov Accelerated Gradient, it uses information accumulated during optimization to guide the parameter perturbation. The authors propose this as a way to obtain low sharpness without significant additional computation or memory compared with SGD or Adam.

The paper evaluates Momentum-SAM in detail and examines separable mechanisms behind Nesterov acceleration, SAM, and the proposed method. This analysis distinguishes effects on training optimization from effects on generalization. The approach matters because it targets the extra work that makes SAM difficult to use with limited computational capacity, while investigating how momentum-based perturbations relate to the benefits of sharpness-aware training.
neurips-2025-momentum-sam-sharpness-awar.tldr: Momentum-SAM uses accumulated momentum to guide sharpness-aware parameter perturbations without significant overhead over SGD or Adam.

paragraphs: MoRE-Brain reconstructs visual experiences from fMRI while making the reconstruction process more interpretable. It organizes processing into a hierarchy of experts, each receiving signals from functionally related groups of brain voxels. This structure is inspired by specialized brain networks and provides a way to examine the contributions of different modeled regions.

The experts first learn to map fMRI signals into a frozen CLIP representation space. A finetuned diffusion model then generates images, with a two-stage routing mechanism adjusting the influence of expert outputs throughout generation. For transfer across subjects, the framework shares the core expert networks and adapts only the subject-specific routers.

The authors report high reconstruction fidelity and use the routing behavior to explain how modeled regions influence semantic and spatial image attributes. Bottleneck analyses further support effective use of the fMRI information rather than excessive dependence on the image generator's prior knowledge. The contribution combines image reconstruction, efficient cross-subject adaptation, and an explicit account of how expert contributions shape the generated result.
neurips-2025-more-brain-routed-mixture-o.tldr: MoRE-Brain routes brain-region expert outputs into image generation to support interpretable fMRI reconstruction and efficient adaptation across subjects.

paragraphs: Human videos could provide a large source of robot-learning experience, but extracting usable action information from them is difficult. This paper represents actions through object-centered three-dimensional motion fields. The representation focuses on how objects move, providing action information for a framework that extracts knowledge from video for zero-shot robot control.

One contribution is a training pipeline for a denoising motion estimator that recovers fine object movements despite noisy depth information. Another is a dense motion-field prediction architecture designed to support transfer between human and robot embodiments and generalization across backgrounds. Together, these components address both the quality of the extracted motion and its usefulness for robot policies.

In real-world experiments, the method reduces 3D motion estimation error by more than 50% relative to the latest method used for comparison. It achieves 55% average task success where prior approaches achieve approximately 10% or less, and demonstrates fine manipulation such as insertion. These results support object-centered motion as a useful representation for transferring action knowledge from human videos.
neurips-2025-object-centric-3d-motion-fi.tldr: Object-centered 3D motion fields transfer manipulation knowledge from human videos, achieving 55% average success in the reported real-world tasks.

paragraphs: Long tasks with infrequent rewards make it difficult for reinforcement learning agents to discover useful behavior. Q-chunking addresses this in offline-to-online learning, where an agent first has access to an existing dataset and then learns through additional interaction. The challenge is to turn that dataset into effective exploration and efficient subsequent learning.

The method treats a sequence of future actions as one action chunk and runs temporal-difference reinforcement learning directly in this chunked action space. This allows the agent to draw on temporally consistent behaviors in the offline data. It also enables unbiased multi-step backups, which the authors use to support more stable and efficient value learning.

Across a range of long-horizon manipulation tasks with sparse rewards, Q-chunking shows strong offline performance and online sample efficiency, outperforming the prior best offline-to-online methods in the reported experiments. Its contribution is a simple recipe for bringing action chunking, already used in imitation learning, into value-based learning in a way that addresses both exploration and training updates.
neurips-2025-reinforcement-learning-with.tldr: Q-chunking learns over action sequences to improve exploration and sample efficiency in offline-to-online reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Recurrent networks repeatedly apply the same weight matrix, so small imbalances can accumulate over long sequences. Glorot initialization is intended to preserve stable signals, but its derivation assumes infinite width and a fixed sequence length. This paper examines what happens when a finite-width linear recurrence instead processes increasingly long sequences.

The authors show that small positive deviations in the matrix's spectral radius can grow through repeated application and cause the hidden state to explode. Their theoretical analysis finds that sequence lengths on the order of the square root of hidden width are sufficient to induce instability. This is a sufficient scale for the demonstrated instability, rather than a claim that every shorter sequence is stable.

To address the problem, the paper proposes a width-aware rescaling of Glorot initialization that places the spectral radius slightly below one, preventing rapid signal growth or decay. The results suggest that initialization theory based on fixed sequence lengths may fail to capture long-range recurrent behavior, motivating theory that explicitly accounts for sequence length and model width together.
neurips-2025-revisiting-glorot-initializ.tldr: The paper shows long-sequence instability in Glorot-initialized linear recurrences and proposes a width-aware rescaling to control signal growth and decay.

paragraphs: Compositional generalization means applying familiar task components in combinations beyond those already learned. This paper asks when ordinary neural networks can acquire that ability despite using continuous, distributed representations. The authors find that increasing both data and model size can produce compositional generalization across different ways of encoding tasks.

A central condition is that the training distribution sufficiently covers the task space. The scaling result therefore depends on what the training data represents. The paper also proves that standard multilayer perceptrons can approximate a general class of compositional task families to arbitrary precision with a neuron count that grows linearly with the number of task modules.

The authors further find that, when networks successfully generalize compositionally, task constituents can be recovered from hidden activations with linear decoding. This provides a measurable relationship between internal representations and compositional behavior. They show that the metric also correlates with failures of text-to-image models to combine known concepts, connecting the analysis to a practical setting where compositional failures remain visible.
neurips-2025-scaling-can-lead-to-composi.tldr: Scaling data and models can yield compositional generalization when training sufficiently covers the task space, with linear decoding revealing relevant internal structure.

paragraphs: Attention becomes expensive as language-model context grows because its computation scales quadratically with sequence length. SeerAttention reduces this burden by learning which blocks of the attention map deserve computation. Its selection adapts to the input context, addressing the rigidity of predefined sparsity patterns and attention-head heuristics.

The method adds a learnable gate inspired by mixture-of-experts routing. It pools query and key tensors along the sequence, processes them with learned linear layers, and multiplies the resulting matrices to score attention blocks. Those scores guide selective block activation. A block-sparse FlashAttention kernel turns the resulting sparsity into GPU speedups.

For pretrained language models, only the gate parameters need training, using a lightweight self-distillation procedure that the authors report converges rapidly. Evaluations show better accuracy and lower latency for long-context prefilling than prior methods. The contribution combines a learned decision about where attention computation is useful with an implementation that can translate that decision into faster processing.
neurips-2025-seerattention-self-distille.tldr: SeerAttention learns context-dependent attention block selection and uses a sparse GPU kernel to improve long-context prefilling accuracy and latency.

paragraphs: Prompt optimization often focuses on instructions tailored to an individual task or query. This paper instead studies optimization of the system prompt, the shared instruction layer used across different tasks. The objective is a system prompt that remains effective across varied user prompts and transfers to tasks not seen during optimization.

The authors formulate this as a bilevel optimization problem and develop a meta-learning framework. It optimizes the system prompt across user prompts from multiple datasets while repeatedly updating those user prompts as well. This joint process aims to make the shared system instructions and task-specific instructions work well together, including when the latter are adapted.

Experiments on fourteen unseen datasets across five domains show that the learned system prompts generalize to diverse user prompts. They also allow test-time user prompts to adapt in fewer optimization steps while achieving better performance. The findings suggest that optimizing shared instructions can improve both transfer and the efficiency of later prompt adaptation in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-system-prompt-optimization-.tldr: Meta-learning system prompts across tasks improves transfer and reduces the user-prompt optimization needed for adaptation in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Neural Processes aim to adapt quickly to new tasks while representing uncertainty from limited observations. They often use a shared latent variable to express uncertainty about the underlying function. This paper empirically finds that the approximate posterior over that variable is frequently miscalibrated, affecting both prediction accuracy and the reliability of uncertainty estimates.

Test Time Scaling for Neural Processes addresses the inference step without changing the pretrained model. It starts with samples from the model's variational approximation and refines them through a Sequential Monte Carlo Sampler. Neural transition kernels repeatedly transform these samples toward a better approximation of the true posterior.

The authors report significant improvements in prediction quality and uncertainty calibration. The approach matters because it uses additional computation at prediction time to improve how an existing model's uncertainty is represented. Its contribution is a sequential inference framework that can refine latent samples after training, helping Neural Processes provide more reliable predictions in settings with limited supervision and a need for calibrated uncertainty.
neurips-2025-test-time-scaling-for-neura.tldr: TTSNPs refine Neural Process latent samples at test time to improve predictions and uncertainty calibration without modifying the pretrained model.

paragraphs: A home-service robot may receive ambiguous instructions while objects are hidden or their locations unknown. Open-ended object types make the range of possibilities even larger. Tru-POMDP addresses this planning problem by combining language-model-generated hypotheses with a probabilistic planner that explicitly tracks uncertainty.

Its Tree of Hypotheses queries a language model hierarchically to construct particle beliefs: collections of possible world states and human goals. An open-ended partially observable Markov decision process then supports Bayesian updates to these beliefs and planning over them. The language model supplies structured possibilities, while the planning framework manages uncertainty among those possibilities as the task proceeds.

Experiments use complex object-rearrangement tasks across diverse kitchen environments. The authors report higher success rates, better plans, greater robustness to ambiguity and occlusion, and more efficient planning than leading language-model and hybrid tree-search planners. These findings support combining structured hypothesis generation with explicit belief tracking when a robot must act without fully knowing either the environment or the intended goal.
neurips-2025-tru-pomdp-task-planning-und.tldr: Tru-POMDP combines hierarchical language-model hypotheses with Bayesian belief-space planning to improve robot task planning under uncertainty.

paragraphs: Neural image watermarking often processes an entire image, making very high resolutions costly in memory and computation. Large images also face cropping and scaling that can make embedded watermarks difficult to recover. This paper proposes an implicit neural representation approach to address both computational demands and robustness to these distortions.

The method generates watermark values pixel by pixel through resolution-independent coordinate sampling. The authors describe this as enabling ultra-high-resolution watermark generation with fixed, limited computational and memory resources. A hierarchical coordinate embedding at multiple scales and a low-rank watermark injection strategy further support image quality and reliable decoding.

Experiments report better robustness and computational efficiency than existing schemes while maintaining high image quality. In the stated 2K-image test, watermark extraction accuracy exceeds 98% when only 0.4% of the image area remains. That result demonstrates strong recovery under severe cropping in the evaluated setting, while the overall framework targets watermarking that remains practical as image resolution increases.
neurips-2025-ultra-high-resolution-water.tldr: Coordinate-based watermark generation supports high-resolution images and achieves over 98% extraction accuracy from 0.4% of image area in the reported 2K test.
